title: SDK First Responder: Debugging Scenarios & Heuristics
summary: Working runbook for first-line responders handling SDK integration failures, unexpected latencies, and telemetry gaps. Focuses on quick repros, prioritized checks, and lightweight fixes to get customers unblocked.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic "first responder" playbook for developer-experience engineers and SEs who get paged or looped into customer SDK integration incidents. The goal: triage fast, restore a reasonable dev experience, and create a minimal repro so platform/infra teams can own deeper fixes.

Audience:
- Developer Experience on-call
- Solutions Engineers doing live debugging
- Support engineers who escalate to eng

How to use:
- Read the triage checklist top-to-bottom for quick wins.
- If unresolved, follow the reproducibility steps and capture the sample payloads/trace ids to attach to tickets.
- Add any new failure patterns encountered to the "Observed Patterns" section (bottom).

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm the customer context: SDK language, integration type (server vs client), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), SDK version.
   - Ask: "Which SDK package and exact version? npm/yarn/pip list output or `pip show`/`npm ls`."
2) Get request identifiers: request_id, trace_id, and any SDK-generated debug id. Ask for a minimal request log line.
3) Check service-level signals: platform incident page, model queueing errors, region health. If platform-level outage, escalate to SRE.
4) If service is green, ask for a reproducible snippet (5 lines) and the exact environment: Node/Python version, OS, network egress rules (VPC?), proxies.
5) Ask customer to enable DEBUG logging in SDK (env var REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 or equivalent) and re-run the failing flow; capture stdout/stderr.
6) If latency issue: request a span sample (start/finish timestamps) and token-level timing if available. Determine whether latency is client-side (DNS, TLS, HTTP) or server-side (inference kernel).

Prioritized fixes (fastest-first):
- Invalid API key / rate limit: check 401/429. If 429, recommend short exponential backoff (retry-after header) and advise customer on quotas.
- Payload shape mismatch: many customer errors come from unexpected JSON shape; validate schema locally.
- Missing streaming hook: when streaming is expected but not attached, SDK may buffer; recommend attaching the `onChunk`/`onPartial` handler.
- TLS or proxy issues: common in private deployments. Verify CA chain and local proxies (mitm), suggest curl test with same proxy env vars.
- Telemetry not showing up: confirm SDK configured with telemetry key and that network egress to telemetry endpoint is allowed.

Minimum reproducibility template (ask customer to fill and run):
- Language: <node|python|go>
- SDK exact version: <x.y.z>
- Short snippet (no credentials):
  ```
  // paste code here
  ```
- Expected result: <short sentence>
- Observed actual: <error/log lines or latency numbers>
- Steps to reproduce: <1,2,3>

Commands to run locally (helpers):
- curl sanity check (replace placeholders):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate
- Node quick repro: `node repro.js` (include instructions to set env vars)
- Python quick repro: `python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python repro.py`

Expected log patterns and what they mean:
- CONNECTED to host (200/204): request reached platform; if no model response, suspect downstream model queueing or runtime failure.
- "KV cache miss" repeated: indicates cold start / cache warming on dedicated pools — advise short burst warmup or prewarm request.
- 502 with HTML body: likely ingress LB returning upstream error; capture full response headers and body.

Telemetry keys to capture (minimum):
- request_id (string)
- trace_id (string)
- sdk_version
- language
- model_id or runtime_id
- region
- token_count
- client_latency_ms
- server_latency_ms
- http_status_code
Record these in the ticket for SRE / infra handoff.

Common failure scenarios & debugging heuristics:
A) Silent truncation / missing content in streaming responses
- Symptom: client receives fewer tokens than expected; no errors.
- Quick checks: confirm streaming handler returned true / didn't throw; verify network middleboxes close idle ws/conn prematurely.
- Workaround: set streaming fallback to chunked polling for 30s; log chunk arrival timestamps.

B) High p95 latency on local dev machines
- Symptom: dev sees 400–800ms p95 on small generation; customer complains dev loop too slow.
- Heuristic: check DNS resolution time, TLS handshake time, and socket connection time (use curl -w or Node diagnostic). Recommend environment variable to disable TLS session reuse for debugging.

C) Authentication flappers across environments
- Symptom: same key works intermittently across CI vs local.
- Heuristic: verify clocks (JWT exp), clock skew with `date -u`, and key rotation windows. Also check request signing libraries for timezone differences.

D) Rate-limit storms after retries
- Symptom: retries amplify 429s, causing backoff thrash.
- Fix: implement jittered exponential backoff and circuit-breaker (sample SDK templates below). Suggest an immediate temporary rate-limited client mode where we surface server-suggested retry-after values.

Temporary mitigations we can suggest customers apply immediately:
- Switch to a lower-traffic model alias (e.g. text-compact) to reduce token load.
- Reduce batch sizes or disable batching during triage.
- Turn on `SDK_DEBUG` and share logs rather than full credentials.

SDK-internal checks we may ask dev team to quick-patch (if customer blocked):
- Add additional debug metadata to every outbound request (short-lived) so we can correlate on-platform.
- Emit a lightweight synthetic span at SDK init to validate network egress path.
- Add defensive parsing around streaming boundary markers to avoid silent drops.

Sample minimal SDK circuit-breaker pseudo-code (deliverable to SEs):
- on 5 consecutive 429/5xx -> open circuit for 60s and return failure with guidance to user; on subsequent requests, try after 60s.
- Keep a sliding window of failures per API key and per region.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Customers sometimes paste stack traces with secrets — remind them to sanitize.
- We should create a small `repro` template repo (node/python) that auto-collects the telemetry keys above and redacts tokens. Low effort and huge lift for debugging. Track as GH issue.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add an SDK feature to auto-upload anonymized debug bundles to a support-only S3? (privacy/regulatory implications)
- How to add a single-line flag in SDKs to toggle verbose telemetry without requiring release (env var vs feature-flip).
- Do we have a consistent cross-language mapping for `request_id` vs `trace_id` fields? sometimes names differ and slows triage.

Observed patterns (add entries here when you see new one):
- 2024-12-05: Repro pattern where private-deploy customers behind enterprise proxy see streaming closures after 10s idle; root cause was proxy killing websocket keepalive. Action: add ws keepalive option + doc.
- 2025-01-22: Customers using older Node 12 runtime see TLS1.3 mismatches leading to occasional handshake failures; recommended upgrade or explicit legacy TLS settings.

Next artifacts to produce (owner: Ava):
- Create repro template repo (GH issue created) — due 2025-02-28.
- Small support-only runbook card in Console with a reproducibility checklist and a button to attach logs to support ticket.
- Short internal training microdoc (15min) for SEs on this playbook.

If you hit something new, add it to the Observed patterns and ping #devexp-triage in Slack with the ticket id.

End of doc.
